subject: Prontera et al. (2011)
object: Prontera et al. (2011) reported acrofrontofacionasal dysostosis type 1 in 2 sisters of Indian origin.

subject: Palagano et al. (2018)
object: Palagano et al. (2018) studied an Indian family with 2 affected sibs diagnosed with acrofrontofacionasal dysostosis type 1. They described it as an extremely rare autosomal recessive syndrome with facial and skeletal abnormalities, short stature, and intellectual disability.

subject: Palagano et al. (2018)
object: In 2 affected sibs from an Indian family with acrofrontofacionasal dysostosis, Palagano et al. (2018) used exome sequencing to identify a novel homozygous truncating mutation in the NBAS gene. Overexpressing the truncated NBAS protein in HEK293T cells impaired both nonsense-mediated decay and Golgi-to-endoplasmic reticulum retrograde traffic.

subject: Palagano et al. (2018)
object: Palagano et al. (2018) found by immunohistochemistry that NBAS protein was expressed in mouse embryos. Expression was seen in developing chondrogenic and osteogenic skeletal structures and in the cortex, hippocampus, and cerebellum. In zebrafish embryos, depleting endogenous z-nbas caused defective morphogenesis of chondrogenic cranial skeletal elements.
